preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)

2. Command Execution:

   - Capture the output of the command.

   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. content.content:
# Moneo Moneo is an open-source personal finance app that runs on your own computer. Import bank statements or sync your bank, track accounts and wealth, plan spending, and ask questions about your money in chat or on a voice call. Figures always come from your own records; the AI explains them and suggests changes that you accept. Website: **[indkhan.github.io/Moneo](https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/)** — screenshots, what Moneo does, and the right installer for your computer. Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital). ## Install ### Desktop preview Desktop installers for Windows, macOS and Linux are attached to [GitHub releases](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/releases) once published (none is published yet; until then, use the source installation below): download, install and open Moneo; nothing else is needed. Settings → App updates installs newer releases and keeps your data. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported. Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed. ### Easiest: let an AI agent install it If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste: > Clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo, then set it up by following .agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md in that repository. If you already downloaded Moneo, open the agent in the Moneo folder and say **"set up Moneo"**. The agent runs the commands, tells you what each step does, and asks you only for what it can't do itself, like installing Docker or entering your keys in Moneo. If it can control your browser or computer, it asks first and then does the clicking too. You type passwords and keys yourself. ### Or install it yourself #### 1. Install the tools - [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) version 22 or newer - [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (on Linux, Docker Engine with Compose) Start Docker Desktop and wait until it says it is running. #### 2. Download Moneo ```sh git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git cd Moneo npm ci ``` #### 3. Run the setup ```sh npm run setup ``` This creates the database in Docker, makes all the passwords and secrets Moneo needs, and saves them in a file called `.env`. The first run downloads a few GB and takes several minutes; you need about 4 GB of free disk space. On Windows a security prompt may ask to install a local certificate: click **Yes** (it is only used for bank connections and only trusted on this computer). You never need to open or edit `.env`. Keep it private and don't delete it. #### 4. Start Moneo ```sh npm run build npm start ``` The build takes a few minutes the first time. Then open **http://localhost:3000**. #### 5. Turn on the AI Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and choose one: - **Sign in with ChatGPT** to use your ChatGPT Go, Plus or Pro plan, - **Sign in with Claude** to use your Claude Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan (see [Use your Claude plan](#use-your-claude-plan-optional)), or - **Paste an OpenAI API key** ([create one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)) and click **Save key**. Usage is billed to that key. Voice calls and dictation need the OpenAI API key. An OpenRouter key is optional (for other models). #### 6. Add your money - **Import** a CSV or Excel export from your bank, or - connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below). That's it. Want it on your phone or tablet too? See [Use it from your phone or tablet](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional). ## Everyday use - **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running). - **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it. - **Update Moneo:** ```sh git pull npm ci npm run setup npm run build npm start ``` Your data and secrets are kept. While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo. Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting. ## Keys and connections Every key and outside service is set up in the app under **Settings → Keys and connections**. Keys are checked with the provider before they are saved, stored encrypted in your database, shown only by their last four characters, and can be replaced or removed at any time. The same section shows that the secrets made by `npm run setup` are in place. ### Use your Claude plan (optional) Moneo can run on your Claude subscription instead of an API key. It uses Claude Code, which comes with Moneo, signed in with your own Claude account on this computer. Moneo never sees or stores your Claude login; Claude Code keeps it, the same one the Claude Code app uses. 1. In **Settings → AI access**, click **Sign in with Claude** on this computer. A Claude sign-in page opens in your browser. 2. Sign in. If the page shows a code, paste it into Moneo and click **Continue**. If you're already signed in to Claude Code, Moneo shows your account straight away; click **Use Claude plan**. Chat, artifacts, briefings, imports and the agents then run on Claude (Opus 5.5 for the chat, Haiku 5.5 for lighter tasks; change them under **Settings → AI and your data → Advanced**). Requests count toward your plan's usage limits, shown at [claude.ai/settings/usage](https://claude.ai/settings/usage). - **Never billed to an API key.** Moneo removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and similar settings before it starts Claude Code, and only runs Claude when Claude Code is signed in with a Claude plan. If you sign out of Claude Code, AI stays off until you sign in again or pick another option. - **Only Moneo's tools.** Claude gets Moneo's finance tools and nothing else: no files, no shell, no other MCP servers, and no chat history saved by Claude Code. Changes still go through cards you accept. - **PDFs in chat** are read on your computer and sent to Claude as text. A scanned PDF has no text to read, so attach photos of its pages instead. - **Not yet:** voice calls and dictation, which still need an OpenAI API key for the audio. - **Stop using Claude** switches Moneo back to ChatGPT or your API key. It doesn't sign you out of Claude Code. - Anthropic's rules say apps may not offer Claude plan sign-in without its approval ([Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)). Moneo only uses the Claude Code login you set up yourself, on your own computer. Decide for yourself whether that fits your use. ### Connect your bank (optional) Moneo syncs booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). It is free for personal use. Each sync is an ordinary import that you can review and undo. 1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create an application in the **Production** environment. 2. Fill in the application form: - Redirect URL: `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` - Privacy policy URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/privacy.html` - Terms of service URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/terms.html` 3. Let the control panel make the key pair, and keep the downloaded private key file (`.pem`). 4. In the control panel, link your own bank accounts to the application. Only linked accounts can be synced. 5. In Moneo, go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks** (also on the Import page). Paste the application ID, paste the private key or upload the `.pem` file, and click **Save and check**. 6. Click **Choose a bank**, pick yours, click **Connect bank** and approve access at your bank. Bank consent usually lasts up to 180 days; Moneo shows a reconnect banner 7 days before it ends. Pending transactions are not synced. If Enable Banking says it rejected the return address, add the Redirect URL from step 2 to your application and try again. ### Connect Scalable Capital (optional) 1. In Scalable on the web, go to **Profile → Security → Agentic Investing** and turn on access (read-only is enough). 2. In Moneo, click **Connect Scalable Capital** under **Settings → Keys and connections** (also on the Import page) and log in to Scalable (with 2FA in the Scalable app). Moneo then reads your holdings, totals and cash every day and shows the portfolio on Wealth. No keys are needed. It also keeps Scalable's own record of your deposits and withdrawals, read in full once after connecting, so money moving between your bank and Scalable counts once on every day of the net worth chart, and a withdrawal that bounced back looks as if the money stayed. Soon after the first sync, a background job works out your portfolio's past value from your Scalable transactions and past prices, so its chart reaches back to your first trade and connecting a portfolio doesn't look like a gain in net worth. Those days are an estimate, saved apart from your real records: prices further than a year back are monthly. Moneo only saves them if replaying your transactions lands on the shares and cash you hold today; otherwise the chart simply starts at your first sync, and it tries again the next day. Disconnecting keeps them, like your synced values, and resetting all data clears them. Artifact Pages and Home cards can show your Scalable portfolio, recent activity and watchlist. By default they use the last sync, the same figures as Wealth. Turn on **Live Scalable data in artifacts** in Settings → AI and your data to read Scalable each time one opens; that also allows quotes, charts and news for any security, but loads slower and needs Scalable to be reachable. ### Use it from your phone or tablet (optional) Your phone becomes another screen on the Moneo running on this computer: same data, same ChatGPT, Claude, bank and Scalable connections. It is off until you turn it on, and nothing changes on this computer. 1. Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet** and click **Turn on**. Moneo tells you if it needs [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download) installed, a sign-in, or one approval for secure addresses. 2. On your phone or tablet, install Tailscale and sign in with the same account. 3. Scan the code in Settings, then choose **Add to Home Screen**. The address and code are your own, from your own Tailscale account. Only devices on your Tailscale network can reach Moneo, and they get in without a password, so don't use a network you share with other people. Leave Tailscale Funnel off: Moneo refuses traffic from the public internet. Moneo then opens like an app. It never keeps your numbers on the phone: when the computer is off, it says so and shows nothing until the computer is back. Keep this computer on and awake with Moneo running: on a laptop, stay plugged in and set closing the lid to do nothing. After a restart, start Docker and run `npm start` again. On Windows, `tailscale set --unattended=true` keeps Tailscale connected after a restart. New ChatGPT, Claude, bank and Scalable logins start on this computer, because those services only return to its address. On Linux, first run `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER`. How it works, step by step: [docs/phone-access-deep-dive.html](docs/phone-access-deep-dive.html). ## Good to know - Moneo only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other devices on your network can't open it unless you turn on [phone and tablet access](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional). - Your data lives in the Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`. `docker compose down` keeps them; **`docker compose down -v` deletes all your data**. - If ports 54321 or 54322 are already in use, add `API_PORT=` and `DB_PORT=` with free ports to `.env` and run `npm run setup` again. ## Development Use `npm run dev` instead of build and start. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for how the project works. | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `npm test` | Unit tests | | `npm run lint` | ESLint | | `npm run build` | Production build | | `npm run test:e2e` | Playwright browser tests (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md)) | Browser tests use a separate QA user, never the owner's workspace: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs` creates it and saves its session, and `--reset` empties its workspace. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Moneo: personal finance on your own computer Skip to content
Moneo
Features Get it Privacy FAQ GitHub
Download

New Moneo Desktop: just install and open it. Download →

Your money, on your computer.
Not someone else's server.

Moneo shows your net worth, syncs your bank and investments, plans what's coming and answers questions about your money. It's open source and runs entirely on your own machine.

↓ Download Moneo View the source on GitHub

Free · Windows, macOS, Linux · MIT licensed

Sample data. Your own numbers never leave your computer.

What it does

Everything about your money, in one private place

Ask

Ask, and it does the work

“Find where I lent money to Bilal and add it.” Moneo searches your transactions, finds the payment and gives you a card to record the loan. “Buy €900 of MSCI World.” It prepares the order on Scalable and shows you exactly what it will cost.

  • Nothing changes until you tap the card
  • Uses your ChatGPT or Claude plan, or your own API key
  • You choose which data the AI may see

Call

Call Moneo and ask several things at once

Tap Call Moneo and just talk. Ask three questions in one breath and Moneo works on all of them in parallel, telling you each answer as it lands. After the call you get a summary, every answer, and any cards to accept.

  • Interrupt, stop a task, or type instead
  • Works from your phone too

Artifacts

Build your own pages and reports

Describe the page you want, like a monthly money story, a subscription radar or a goals tracker, and Moneo builds it from your data. Keep it, refine it in chat, and pin it to your Home as a card.

  • Always shows your latest numbers
  • Runs in a sandbox with no internet access

Your Home

Widgets you design yourself

“Add a card that tracks my eating out against my budget.” Moneo turns any artifact into a Home widget that sits next to the built-in ones: net worth, budgets, goals and what's coming up. Arrange Home the way you want it.

  • Small, medium or large
  • Updates with your data every time you open Home

Wealth

Your net worth, traced

Bank accounts, your Scalable Capital portfolio with every holding and its gains, money friends owe you, and assets and debts you add yourself: one number with a year of history, and where every change came from.

  • Bank sync through Enable Banking (Europe)
  • Or import CSV and Excel statements, with undo

Plan

Goals, budgets and what's coming

Set goals like a house deposit or a trip, and Moneo tells you when you'll get there at your monthly plan. It finds your recurring payments, forecasts your cash and tracks your budgets.

  • Earmark savings for each goal
  • Try “what if” scenarios safely

Phone

On your phone too, still private

Turn on phone access and open Moneo from your own phone and tablet over Tailscale, a free private network for your devices. Add it to your home screen like an app. Your data stays on your computer.

Get it

Two ways to run it

Same app, same features. Changes to the code reach both.

Download the app

For everyone. Install it and open it: no Docker, Node.js or terminal. Updates come from Settings → App updates.

  1. Download Moneo for your computer below.
  2. Open it. The first start sets up your private database (about a minute).
  3. Add your AI in Settings, then import a statement or connect your bank.
↓ Download

Run from the source

For developers who want to read or change the code. Needs Git, Node.js 22 or newer and Docker.

git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
npm run setup
npm run build
npm start
Read the setup guide

Download

Get Moneo for your computer

Looking up the latest release…

WindowsWindows 10 and 11, 64-bit macOS, Apple siliconM1 and newer macOS, IntelIntel Macs Linux AppImageMost distributions, updates itself Linux .debDebian and Ubuntu
Your computer may warn you the first time

The installers aren't code-signed yet, so your system doesn't recognise the publisher. You can check each file against SHA256SUMS.txt in the release.

  • Windows: if “Windows protected your PC” appears, choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • macOS: right-click Moneo in Applications, choose Open, then Open again.
  • Linux AppImage: make it executable (chmod +x Moneo-*.AppImage), then run it.

Privacy

Built so your data stays yours

No account, no cloud

Moneo runs on your computer. There is no Moneo server and no sign-up.

Only what you connect

Data goes only to your AI provider, and your bank or Scalable if you connect them. No analytics, no tracking.

Numbers come from code

Money is stored exactly, in its currency. The AI explains and proposes; it never quietly changes your data.

Nothing is lost

Imports and changes can be undone, and the desktop app backs up your data every day.

FAQ

Questions

Is Moneo free?

Yes. Moneo is free and open source under the MIT license. The AI uses your own ChatGPT or Claude plan or an API key, so any AI costs are between you and your provider.

Does any of my financial data go online?

Only to services you connect yourself: your AI provider when you ask a question, Enable Banking to sync your bank, and Scalable Capital for investments. Everything else stays in the database on your computer.

What's the difference between the app and running from source?

None in features. The app bundles everything, the database included, so you just install it. Running from source is for people who want to change the code; it uses Docker for the database.

Can I use it on my phone?

Yes. Turn on phone access in Settings and connect your phone with Tailscale. Moneo stays on your computer; your phone opens it from there.

How do updates work?

In the app, open Settings → App updates and choose Check for updates. On Windows and Linux (AppImage) Moneo installs the update and restarts with your data. On a Mac it opens the download. From source: git pull, npm ci, npm run setup, npm run build, then npm start.

Which banks work?

Banks available through Enable Banking, which covers many banks across Europe. Any bank works through statement import.

Take your finances back home.

↓ Download Moneo Star on GitHub

Moneo only saves them if replaying your transactions lands on the shares and cash you hold today; otherwise the chart simply starts at your first sync, and it tries again the next day. Your money, on your computer.
Not someone else's server.

Moneo shows your net worth, syncs your bank and investments, plans what's coming and answers questions about your money. It's open source and runs entirely on your own machine.

Free · Windows, macOS, Linux · MIT licensed

Sample data. Your own numbers never leave your computer.

What it does

Everything about your money, in one private place

Ask

Ask, and it does the work

“Find where I lent money to Bilal and add it.” Moneo searches your transactions, finds the payment and gives you a card to record the loan. “Buy €900 of MSCI World.” It prepares the order on Scalable and shows you exactly what it will cost.

  • Nothing changes until you tap the card
  • Uses your ChatGPT or Claude plan, or your own API key
  • You choose which data the AI may see

Call

Call Moneo and ask several things at once

Tap Call Moneo and just talk. Ask three questions in one breath and Moneo works on all of them in parallel, telling you each answer as it lands. After the call you get a summary, every answer, and any cards to accept.

  • Interrupt, stop a task, or type instead
  • Works from your phone too

Artifacts

Build your own pages and reports

Describe the page you want, like a monthly money story, a subscription radar or a goals tracker, and Moneo builds it from your data. Keep it, refine it in chat, and pin it to your Home as a card.

  • Always shows your latest numbers
  • Runs in a sandbox with no internet access

Your Home

Widgets you design yourself

“Add a card that tracks my eating out against my budget.” Moneo turns any artifact into a Home widget that sits next to the built-in ones: net worth, budgets, goals and what's coming up. Arrange Home the way you want it.

  • Small, medium or large
  • Updates with your data every time you open Home

Wealth

Your net worth, traced

Bank accounts, your Scalable Capital portfolio with every holding and its gains, money friends owe you, and assets and debts you add yourself: one number with a year of history, and where every change came from.

  • Bank sync through Enable Banking (Europe)
  • Or import CSV and Excel statements, with undo

Plan

Goals, budgets and what's coming

Set goals like a house deposit or a trip, and Moneo tells you when you'll get there at your monthly plan. It finds your recurring payments, forecasts your cash and tracks your budgets.

  • Earmark savings for each goal
  • Try “what if” scenarios safely

Phone

On your phone too, still private

Turn on phone access and open Moneo from your own phone and tablet over Tailscale, a free private network for your devices. Add it to your home screen like an app. Your data stays on your computer.

Get it

Two ways to run it

Same app, same features. Changes to the code reach both.

Download the app

For everyone. Install it and open it: no Docker, Node.js or terminal. Updates come from Settings → App updates.

  1. Download Moneo for your computer below.
  2. Open it. The first start sets up your private database (about a minute).
  3. Add your AI in Settings, then import a statement or connect your bank.

For developers who want to read or change the code. Needs Git, Node.js 22 or newer and Docker.

git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
npm run setup
npm run build
npm start

Get Moneo for your computer

Looking up the latest release…

WindowsWindows 10 and 11, 64-bit macOS, Apple siliconM1 and newer macOS, IntelIntel Macs Linux AppImageMost distributions, updates itself Linux .debDebian and Ubuntu
Your computer may warn you the first time

Built so your data stays yours

No account, no cloud

Moneo runs on your computer. There is no Moneo server and no sign-up.

Only what you connect

Data goes only to your AI provider, and your bank or Scalable if you connect them. No analytics, no tracking.

Numbers come from code

Money is stored exactly, in its currency. The AI explains and proposes; it never quietly changes your data.

Nothing is lost

Imports and changes can be undone, and the desktop app backs up your data every day.

FAQ

Questions

Is Moneo free?

Yes. Moneo is free and open source under the MIT license. The AI uses your own ChatGPT or Claude plan or an API key, so any AI costs are between you and your provider.

Does any of my financial data go online?

Only to services you connect yourself: your AI provider when you ask a question, Enable Banking to sync your bank, and Scalable Capital for investments. Everything else stays in the database on your computer.

What's the difference between the app and running from source?

None in features. The app bundles everything, the database included, so you just install it. Running from source is for people who want to change the code; it uses Docker for the database.

Can I use it on my phone?

Yes. Turn on phone access in Settings and connect your phone with Tailscale. Moneo stays on your computer; your phone opens it from there.

Which banks work?

Banks available through Enable Banking, which covers many banks across Europe. Any bank works through statement import.

# Moneo Desktop

An Electron app that runs Moneo with its own private database on the owner's computer: no Docker,
Node.js, terminal or `.env`. The source setup (`npm run setup`, `npm run dev`) is unchanged.

## Build

```sh
node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform win-x64   # native backend + mkcert → desktop/.build (see that script)
npm run desktop:build                    # Next.js standalone server + migrations → desktop/.build, main process → desktop/dist
npm run desktop:dev                      # run Electron on the unpacked build
npm run desktop:dist                     # installers → desktop/release (Windows NSIS, macOS dmg+zip, Linux AppImage+deb)
npm run desktop:smoke                    # drive the packaged app (desktop/release/*-unpacked) end to end
```

`desktop:build` runs `next build` with `MONEO_DESKTOP_BUILD=1` (standalone output in `.next-desktop/`, so
`.next` is untouched) and every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable unset. It refuses to run when a `.env*` file
in the checkout sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` (Next.js would bake those addresses in), and fails if a local
Supabase address ends up in the output anyway.

Packages are unsigned by default. With `CSC_LINK` and `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` set, electron-builder signs;
on macOS `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` and `APPLE_TEAM_ID` also notarize. Unsigned macOS
builds get an ad-hoc signature. Package each platform on that platform (`npm run desktop:dist -- --win`,
`--mac`, `--linux`); the macOS and Linux backend needs a native addon built there.

## Where things live

- Package: `app.asar` holds only `dist/`, `setup/` and the icon. Next to it: `app/` (Next server),
  `migrations/`, `bootstrap/`, `backend/<os>-<arch>/`, `storage-api/`.
- Per user: the Electron user-data folder (`MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` overrides it): `config.json` (backend
  secrets), `shell.json` (app port, tray notice, last backup), `postgres/`, `storage/`, `data/`
  (ChatGPT sign-in, bank certificate), `backups/`, `logs/`, `chromium/` (the window's own cookies).

The app listens on `http://localhost:47300` (chosen once, then kept: phone access, Scalable's return
address and ChatGPT's callback name it). If it is taken on the first run, a free port is saved instead.

## Behaviour

- Start: a small status window shows each step (the first run says it is creating a private database),
  then the app window opens Home. On failure it offers Try again, Open logs folder, Restore from backup, Quit.
- Closing the window keeps Moneo in the tray, so background syncs and phone access keep working.
  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it
  to the front; the browser tab says to continue in Moneo. The server reaches the window through a
  loopback address that is random for each launch and refuses browser requests (`src/bridge.ts`);
  if the window cannot take it, the browser shows the result as in a source checkout. Every other address also goes to the browser
  (https only). The window allows only the microphone and copying, for Moneo's own pages.
- Updates: Settings → App updates checks the newest published GitHub release only when the owner
  asks (`src/updates.ts`, electron-updater). On Windows and with the AppImage, Update downloads it,
  quits Moneo cleanly, installs it and starts Moneo again; data stays in the user folder, and a pending
  migration makes a `pre-upgrade` backup first. macOS (unsigned) and `.deb` installs open the release
  page to download instead. Draft and pre-releases are never offered. `npm run desktop:dist` writes
  the `latest*.yml` files the check reads; the release workflow uploads them with the installers.

## Releasing

Releases are made only from a `v*` tag; pull request runs keep their installers as workflow
artifacts for 7 days and never create a release.

1. Bump `desktop/package.json`'s version on `main` (the first release is `0.1.0` as is).
2. Tag and push: `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.
3. The Desktop workflow builds every platform and drafts a release with the installers, `latest*.yml`,
   blockmaps and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
4. Publish the draft on GitHub. Drafts are invisible to visitors, to the landing page's download
   button and to Settings → App updates; once published, all three offer it.

### Bank return certificate

Enable Banking returns to `https://localhost:3443`. On every start Moneo makes that certificate with the
bundled mkcert if it is missing (its signing authority lives in the user folder, `mkcert/`); nothing is
trusted yet. The first time the owner opens a bank's consent page, Moneo explains why and asks the
computer to trust that authority once: Windows shows its own confirmation (current user's store),
macOS asks for the login keychain password, Linux adds it to the browsers' NSS store (needs `certutil`).

## Security fuses

For a private copied-data preview, launch the desktop executable with `MONEO_DESKTOP_PREVIEW=1`.
This runtime-only flag prevents persisted Workflow recovery, the scheduler and the bank callback
listener from starting, and skips automatic bank/Scalable sync when opening a page. It does not
block network requests triggered by explicit actions in the app, and is
not an offline mode. Normal desktop launches and source development keep their usual behavior.

RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` are off; cookie encryption, asar-only loading and embedded asar
integrity are on. The smoke test reads them back from the packaged executable. Because `--inspect` is off,
Playwright's `_electron.launch` cannot attach, so the smoke test drives the app over
`--remote-debugging-port` instead. DevTools are off in packaged builds unless `MONEO_DESKTOP_DEBUG=1`.
