    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      # No setup-go: fetch-backend.mjs downloads its own pinned Go toolchain into desktop/.cache.
      - run: npm ci

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: desktop/.cache
          key: desktop-cache-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs') }}

      - name: Fetch the native backend
        run: node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform ${{ matrix.id }}

      - run: npm run desktop:build

      - name: Package
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          WIN_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_LINK }}
          WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          # Secrets that do not exist arrive as empty strings; unset them so electron-builder
          # treats the build as unsigned.
          for name in CSC_LINK CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID WIN_CSC_LINK WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then unset "$name"; fi
          done
          if [ -z "${CSC_LINK:-}" ] && [ -z "${WIN_CSC_LINK:-}" ]; then
            export CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false
            echo "No signing certificate: building unsigned packages."
          fi
          npm run desktop:dist -- ${{ matrix.builder }} --publish never
          # Both Mac jobs write latest-mac.yml. Macs only read the version from it (unsigned apps
          # download from the release page), so the Apple Silicon one is kept.
          if [ "${{ matrix.id }}" = "mac-x64" ]; then rm -f desktop/release/latest-mac.yml; fi

      - name: List packages
        run: ls -la desktop/release

      # The smoke test starts the unpacked app (own temporary home, no cloud calls).
      - name: Linux dependencies for the smoke test
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libnss3-tools
          # Ubuntu 24.04 blocks the unprivileged user namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs.
          sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

content.text:
PR #214 is open: https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/214. The v0.1.2 release isn't out yet: its Mac builds are being re-run now, and I'll publish the release if they pass.

**What I did as a new user:** I downloaded the Windows installer from the landing page and its checksum matched. I ran the released v0.1.1 app with its own data folder, so your Moneo wasn't touched. I turned on AI with your Claude plan, imported a sample bank CSV, and the agent team then ran by itself. That basic path works.

**What the PR fixes:**
1. **Mac downloads:** the latest release (v0.1.1) has no Mac installer, but the Mac buttons on the landing page led to a release page without one. They now say "Not in this release yet" and point to running from source.
2. **README:** it still said no release was published. It now starts with the download.
3. **Settings in the desktop app:** it told people to run `npm run setup` and use a `.env` file, neither of which exists in the app. That text now only shows for source installs.
4. **Bank country list:** only 11 countries were listed, as two-letter codes, so people in Sweden, Poland, Norway and other countries couldn't find their bank. It now lists all 29 countries Enable Banking serves, by name, and starts on the user's own country.
5. **Enable Banking setup:** the instructions were one dense sentence. They're now five numbered steps that say the setup is free and takes about 10 minutes.
6. **Landing page FAQ and steps:** they now say any bank works through statement import, and that bank sync is an optional one-time setup.

**From the Enable Banking changelog:** two items were useful. Moneo now warns that some banks ask you to approve twice (for example in Italy, where it's needed for history older than 90 days). The README also gives their new support address for personal-use apps, where an AI assistant answers. The new banks in Sweden, Norway and Denmark only became reachable through fix 4. The other changelog items don't affect Moneo.

**Checks:** lint and typecheck pass. In the full unit test run, 1560 passed and two failed on timeouts, in files this PR doesn't touch; both pass when run alone. Nothing here overlaps the open PRs #204–#211.

**Mac release:** the v0.1.2 tag already existed. Its build failed on both Macs because Apple's signing check (`codesign`) rejected the app: "invalid destination for symbolic link in bundle". A pull request build made after the same Mac fix passed on both Macs, so I think the failure came from a stale build cache, but I haven't confirmed that. If the re-run fails again, there's a real bundling bug to fix first, and I'll ask you before going further.

I didn't test phone access or connect a real bank or Scalable, because those would touch your own accounts.

lines: Download the installer for your computer from the [website](https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/#download) or [GitHub releases](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/releases), install it and open Moneo; nothing else is needed. Windows and Linux installers are published; macOS arrives with the next release (until then, use the source installation below). Home then shows three first steps: turn on AI, add your money, run the agent team. Settings → App updates installs newer releases and keeps your data. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported.

Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed.

+Chat can also answer questions no built-in tool covers by running a read-only SQL query over your finance records. It runs as you, only within your own data and AI data scopes, can't change anything, and can't see stored bank or Scalable tokens, AI keys or settings; each query is shown under the answer's tools.
### Easiest: let an AI agent install it
If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste:

- **Never billed to an API key.** Moneo removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and similar settings before it starts Claude Code, and only runs Claude when Claude Code is signed in with a Claude plan. If you sign out of Claude Code, AI stays off until you sign in again or pick another option.

- **Only Moneo's tools.** Claude gets Moneo's finance tools and nothing else: no files, no shell, no other MCP servers, and no chat history saved by Claude Code. Changes still go through cards you accept.
-- **PDFs in chat** are read on your computer and sent to Claude as text. A scanned PDF has no text to read, so attach photos of its pages instead.
- **Not yet:** voice calls and dictation, which still need an OpenAI API key for the audio.
- **Stop using Claude** switches Moneo back to ChatGPT or your API key. It doesn't sign you out of Claude Code.

- Anthropic's rules say apps may not offer Claude plan sign-in without its approval ([Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)). Moneo only uses the Claude Code login you set up yourself, on your own computer. Decide for yourself whether that fits your use.
- Moneo only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other devices on your network can't open it unless you turn on [phone and tablet access](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional).

+- **Files in chat:** attach photos, PDFs, Word (DOCX), PowerPoint (PPTX), Excel (XLSX) or CSV files, up to four of 25 MB each. Documents are turned into text on your computer, the same way for every AI source; scanned PDF pages are sent as images. Answers show small chips such as `statement.pdf · p.3` that open the page, slide, paragraph or cell they came from.
- Your data lives in the Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`. `docker compose down` keeps them; **`docker compose down -v` deletes all your data**.
- If ports 54321 or 54322 are already in use, add `API_PORT=` and `DB_PORT=` with free ports to `.env` and run `npm run setup` again.

git add -A && git commit -qm "Fix Mac release builds failing codesign on bundled symlinks

Every tagged release so far failed on macOS. After #206 fixed the entitlements
path, codesign rejected the app with \"invalid destination for symbolic link in
bundle\". The desktop build now replaces each symlink in desktop/.build with a
copy of its target (dropping broken ones) and logs which. Pull request runs
now sign Mac builds ad hoc too, so codesign problems show up before a tag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -qu origin t3/mac-release-symlinks 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:" ; gh pr create --base main --head t3/mac-release-symlinks --title "Fix Mac release builds failing codesign on bundled symlinks" --body "No Moneo release has a macOS installer yet: every \`v*\` tag build failed on both Mac jobs. #206 fixed the first failure, the entitlements path. The v0.1.2 build (re-run today) then failed at \`codesign --verify\`:

\`\`\`
Moneo.app: invalid destination for symbolic link in bundle
\`\`\`

PR builds never showed this because electron-builder skips signing on pull requests.

## Changes
- \`scripts/desktop/build.mjs\` replaces every symlink in \`desktop/.build\` with a copy of its target before packaging, and drops broken links. Each one is logged, so the CI log names the culprit. These are library aliases in the native backend, so the copies cost a few MB.
- \`.github/workflows/desktop.yml\` sets \`CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST=true\`. PR runs now sign Mac builds ad hoc and run the same codesign checks as a release.

## Checks
- This PR's own Mac jobs are the test: they now sign and verify.
- \`node --check\` and eslint pass on the script.

## After merge
Move the \`v0.1.2\` tag to the merge commit, or bump the version to 0.1.3 and tag that, then publish the drafted release. The landing page's Mac buttons then work.
